State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Reliance Retail Ltd. vs Sh. Bhawan Kumar. & Anr. on 3 April, 2019
H. P. STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL
 COMMISSION SHIMLA
 First Appeal No. : 262/2017
 Date of Presentation: 05.10.2017
 Order Reserved on : 05.12.2018
 Date of Order : 03.04.2019
 ......
Reliance Retail Limited r/o Mohal/Mauza Bira Tehsil and
District Kangra H.P. -176001.

 ...... Appellant/Opposite Party No.2

 Versus

1. Shri Bhawan Kumar Son of Late Shri Tulsi Ram Village
 and Post Office Serathana Tehsil Nagrota Bagwan District
 Kangra H.P.-176056.
 ......Respondent/Complainant

2. Shri Anand Prakash & Sons Opposite Govt. Sr. Secondary
 School (Boys) Nagrota Bagwan Tehsil Nagrota Bagwan
 District Kangra H.P. -176047

 ......Respondent/Opposite party No.1

Coram

Hon'ble Justice P.S. Rana (R) President
Hon'ble Mr. Vijay Pal Khachi Member
Hon'ble Ms. Sunita Sharma Member

Whether approved for reporting?1 Yes.

For Appellant : Mr. Raj Negi Advocate.
For Respondent No.1 : In person.
For Respondent No.2 : None.

JUSTICE P.S. RANA (R) PRESIDENT:

O R D E R :
-
1. Present appeal is filed under
section 15
of

Consumer Protection Act 1986 against order dated
1
Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the order? Yes.
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

05.09.2017 passed by Learned District Forum in consumer

complaint No.43/2017 titled Bhawan Kumar Versus Anand

Prakash & Sons & Anr.
Brief facts of Matter:
2. Complainant filed consumer complaint under
Section 12
of Consumer Protection Act 1986 pleaded therein

that complainant purchased mobile phone handset LYF

(LS5017) on dated 27.10.2016 at the cost of Rs.8500/- (Eight

thousand five hundred) from opposite party No.1. It is pleaded

that on dated 23.03.2017 when complainant switched on the

mobile phone it was found that mobile phone was out of

order. It is further pleaded that thereafter complainant visited

the dealer and requested the dealer to find out the fault. It is

further pleaded that thereafter dealer sent the mobile phone

handset to Reliance Service Center Kangra to find out fault. It

is further pleaded that Reliance Service Center Kangra

returned the mobile phone handset and intimated that device

was dead due to liquid logged and demanded amount of

Rs.6812.22/- (Six thousand eight hundred twelve rupees and

twenty two paisa) for its repair. It is further pleaded that

defect occurred during the warranty period. Complainant

sought relief of replacement of mobile phone without any

costs. Prayer for acceptance of consumer complaint sought.
2
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)
3. Learned District Forum proceeded ex-parte

against opposite party No.1 on dated 16.05.2017.
4. Per contra version filed on behalf of opposite party

No.2 pleaded therein that present consumer complaint is not

maintainable. It is pleaded that warranty was subject to

warranty terms and conditions relating to product. It is

further pleaded that after verification of product it was found

that product was liquid logged. It is further pleaded that

liquid logged does not fall within the warranty condition as

per warranty card and complainant was informed to bear the

cost of repair. It is further pleaded that complainant insisted

for free repair of mobile handset. It is further pleaded that

representative of complainant took back mobile phone

handset and left the premises of opposite party No.2. It is

further pleaded that opposite party No.2 did not commit any

deficiency in service. Prayer for dismissal of consumer

complaint sought.
5. Learned District Forum partly allowed the

complaint and ordered opposite parties to jointly and severally

replace the defective mobile phone handset of the

complainant with a new one of the same price. Learned

District Forum further ordered that in alternative opposite

parties would refund amount of Rs.8500/- (Eight thousand

five hundred) to the complainant within a period of thirty days
3
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

w.e.f. 05.09.2017. Learned District Forum further ordered

that in addition opposite parties would pay compensation to

the complainant to the tune of Rs.5000/- (Five thousand) for

harassment.
6. Feeling aggrieved against order passed by learned

District Forum Reliance Retail Ltd./opposite party No.2 filed

present appeal before State Commission.
7. We have heard learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellant and we have also heard co-respondent

No.1 in person and we have also perused entire record

carefully. None appeared on behalf of co-respondent No.2.
8. Following points arise for determination in present

appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by Reliance Retail Ltd. is
 liable to be accepted as mentioned in
 memorandum of grounds of appeal and whether
 liquid logged problem in the mobile phone handset
 falls within the exclusion clause of warranty
 condition?
2. Final order.
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
9. Complainant filed affidavit Ex.CW-1 in evidence.
There is recital in affidavit that deponent purchased mobile

phone handset LYF (LS5017) on dated 27.10.2016 at the cost
4
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

of Rs.8500/- (Eight thousand five hundred) from opposite

party No.1 who is authorized dealer of opposite party No.2.

There is further recital in affidavit that on dated 23.03.2017

when deponent switched on the mobile phone it was found

that mobile phone was out of order due to some defect in the

mobile phone. There is further recital in affidavit that

thereafter deponent visited the office of opposite party No.1

and requested opposite party No.1 to find out fault. There is

further recital in affidavit that thereafter opposite party No.1

sent mobile phone handset to Reliance Service Center Kangra

to find out fault. There is further recital in affidavit that

Reliance Service Center Kangra returned mobile phone

handset and intimated that device was dead due to liquid

logged and demanded amount of Rs.6812.22/- (Six thousand

eight hundred twelve rupees and twenty two paisa) for its

repair. There is further recital in affidavit that defect occurred

during the warranty period and it is the legal duty of opposite

party No.2 to repair the mobile phone handset free of charges

or to replace original mobile phone handset during warranty

period.
10. Opposite party No.2 filed affidavit of Amit Arora

Ex.OPW2-1 in evidence. There is recital in the affidavit that

after depositing the product by representative of complainant

opposite party No.2 created a job sheet and after inspection
5
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

and verification of the product opposite party No.2 found that

product was liquid logged. There is further recital in affidavit

that liquid logged product does not fall within warranty item

mentioned in the warranty card. There is further recital in

affidavit that complainant refused to pay the repair charges of

the product and insisted for free repair of product. There is

further recital in affidavit that there was no manufacturing

defect in the product and no expert report placed on record

relating to manufacturing defect.
11. Opposite party No.2 also filed affidavit of Anku

Goswami Ex.OPW2-2 in evidence. There is recital in the

affidavit that deponent is Center Manager Service of opposite

party No.2. There is further recital in affidavit that on dated

24.03.2017 representative of complainant visited the office of

opposite party No.2 and reported about non-functioning of the

mobile phone. There is further recital in affidavit that job

sheet was also prepared. There is further recital in affidavit

that after inspection and verification of the product personally

by deponent it was found that product was liquid logged and

there is further recital in the affidavit that remark was noted

by the deponent personally in job card as "Liquid Logged".

There is further recital in affidavit that product suffering from

liquid logged was outside the purview of warranty card for free

repair. There is further recital in affidavit that representative
6
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

of complainant refused to pay the repair charges and left the

premises of opposite party No.2 alongwith defective mobile

phone handset.
12. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of appellant Reliance Retail Ltd. that mobile phone was

suffering from liquid logged problem and liquid logged

problem does not fall within warranty condition and on this

ground appeal be allowed is decided accordingly. It is proved

on record that warranty card was issued by the manufacturer

to the complainant at the time of sale by authorized dealer.

State Commission has carefully perused the terms and

conditions of the warranty card Annexure C-4. As per terms

and conditions of warranty card Annexure C-4 company

would not be obliged to undertake repairs of product affected

by water/liquid seepage. Annexure C-4 was filed by

complainant himself before the learned District Forum and

complainant could not be allowed to approbate and reprobate

the terms and conditions of warranty card.
13. As per terms and conditions of warranty card

Annexure C-4 complainant is not legally entitled for repair of

mobile phone free of charges qua liquid logged problem. State

Commission is of the opinion that terms and conditions of the

warranty card are binding upon both the parties and no party

could be allowed to approbate and reprobate terms and
7
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

conditions of the warranty card. State Commission has also

carefully perused the retail invoice. As per retail invoice

mobile phone handset was purchased on dated 27.10.2016 by

complainant from opposite party No.1 who is authorized

dealer of Reliance Retail Ltd. in consideration amount of

Rs.8500/- (Eight thousand five hundred). Retail invoice is

signed by complainant and seller. There is recital in the

invoice bill that (1) Goods once sold would not be taken back

or exchanged (2) Warranty on handsets would be provided by

the manufactures/authorized Service Centres. State

Commission is of the opinion that terms and conditions of the

invoice bill are binding upon complainant because invoice bill

has been signed by complainant in English language and

complainant could not be allowed to approbate and reprobate

terms and conditions of invoice bill for his personal benefit.
14. Complainant did not place on record expert report

in order to prove that there was manufacturing defect in the

mobile set. It is well settled law that manufacturing defect in

the product could be proved only by way of opinion of expert.

See 2017 (1) CPR 643 NC Bhagwan Singh Shekhawat Versus

M/s. R.K. Photostat & Communication & Ors. See 2017 (3)

CPR 35 NC Mahender Kumar Versus Hero Honda Motors Ltd.

& Anr. Hence it is held that manufacturing defect is not

proved by the complainant.
8
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)
15. Anku Goswami who is Center Manager and

professional in service of Reliance Limited has specifically

mentioned in his personal affidavit that he personally created

a job card and after personal inspection and verification of

mobile set in question by him it was found that mobile set

was suffering from liquid logged. Affidavit filed by Anku

Goswami is trustworthy, reliable and inspires confidence of

State Commission. There is no evidence on record in order to

prove that Anku Goswami has hostile animus against the

complainant at any point of tome. Complainant did not place

on record any counter expert report that mobile handset was

not damaged due to liquid logged. Affidavit filed by Anku

Goswami that mobile set in question was suffering from liquid

logged remained unrebutted on record. Liquid logged problem

falls within the exclusion clause of warranty card submitted

by complainant himself before learned District Forum as

Annexure C-4.
16. Submission of complainant that order of learned

District Forum is in accordance with law and in accordance

with proved facts and same be affirmed and appeal filed by

appellant Reliance Retail Ltd. be dismissed is decided

accordingly. Plea of complainant that there was

manufacturing defect in the mobile set is defeated on the

concept of ipse-dixit (An assertion made without proof).
9
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

Complainant did not adduce any expert evidence on record in

order to prove that mobile set was suffering from

manufacturing defect.
17. Plea of complainant that mobile set was not

suffering from liquid logged problem is also defeated on the

concept of ipse-dixit (An assertion made without proof).

Complainant did not adduce any counter affidavit of expert in

order to prove that mobile set in question was not suffering

from liquid logged problem. State Commission is of the

opinion that in liquid logged problem matter in mobile set

complainant is under legal obligation to pay repair charges to

the opposite parties. State Commission is of the opinion that

liquid logged problem occurred in the mobile set due to

personal fault of complainant and it is well settled law that

person who seeks equity must do equity himself. State

Commission is of the opinion that opposite parties are not

under legal obligation to repair the fault free of costs which

fault occurred in the mobile set in question due to fault of

complainant himself personally.
18. Sole affidavit of complainant is not sufficient

because complainant is personally interested person in the

present matter as complainant has filed consumer complaint

against the opposite parties personally. Complainant did not

file any corroborative affidavit of independent person in order
10
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

to prove that mobile phone was not suffering from liquid

logged problem. Corroborative evidence of independent

witness on behalf of complainant was essential in the present

matter. Point No.1 is decided accordingly.

Point No.2: Final Order
19. In view of findings upon point No.1 above appeal

filed by Reliance Retail Ltd. is partly allowed. Order of learned

District Forum that opposite parties would jointly and

severally replace defective mobile phone handset of

complainant with new one of same price or in alternative

opposite parties would refund amount of Rs.8500/- (Eight

thousand five hundred) to the complainant within a period of

thirty days from the date of order passed by learned District

Forum is set aside. Order of learned District Forum that

opposite parties would pay compensation to the complainant

to the tune of Rs.5000/- (Five thousand) for harassment is

also set aside.
20. It is further ordered that appellant/opposite party

No.2 shall repair defect in the mobile phone handset within

thirty days after receipt of certified copy of order on usual

charges approved by manufacturing company to the

satisfaction of complainant and thereafter complainant shall

pay usual charges of repair within one month of repair of
11
Reliance Retail Ltd. Versus Bhawan Kumar & Anr. (F.A. No.262/2017)

mobile phone handset in question. Terms and Conditions of

warranty Annexure C-4, retail invoice bill dated 27.10.2016

Annexure C-1 issued by opposite party No.1 and job sheet

dated 27.03.2017 Annexure C-3 shall form part and parcel of

order. Parties are left to bear their own litigation costs before

State Commission. File of learned District Forum alongwith

certified copy of order be sent back forthwith and file of State

Commission be consigned to record room after due

completion forthwith. Certified copy of order be transmitted to

parties forthwith free of costs strictly as per rules. Appeal is

disposed of. Pending application(s) if any also disposed of.
Justice P.S. Rana (R)
 President

 Vijay Pal Khachi
 Member

 Sunita Sharma
 Member
03.04.2019.
